Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposal so we have a single place to align:

What we saw
- Retrieval + contextualized scoring flows are great fit for your agent use case; hallucination surface is low on the curated prompt set.
- Two bottlenecks to consider: (1) peak text-generation latency for 2k-context summaries and (2) per-request unit cost at expected QPS when using the highest-quality engine.

Proposed model slate (shortlist rationale) — we recommend testing these three in the pilot:
1) RW-13B-q4: best cost/latency mix for your throughput. Lower token cost and consistent 90ms median for 512-token outputs on A100s.
2) OpenLlama-30B-int8: higher quality on long-context summarization (+0.6 QA F1 in our prompt set) but ~2x token cost and 250–350ms median latency at your expected QPS. Good fallback when quality spikes matter.
3) Mistral-7B-v2-8bit: smallest footprint, very low latency (<60ms median) for short answers and cheap for scale, but lower pass@1 on nuanced QA.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Quality vs cost: OpenLlama-30B-int8 wins quality on edge cases; RW-13B-q4 reduces ops costs and keeps latency predictable.
- Fallback strategy: route standard traffic to RW-13B-q4, route flagged/low-confidence prompts to OpenLlama-30B-int8.
- Regression concerns: we'll run regression guards with your baseline prompt set (attached). We recommend automatic rollback on a 3% drop in hallucination precision or 5% drop in key NPS proxies.

Next steps
- Deliverables (this week): bench CSV, prompt pack v1, canary rollout playbook (attached).
- Pilot proposal: 2-week pilot starting when you sign off (we'll run RW-13B-q4 primary, OpenLlama-30B-int8 as canary).
- Action owners:
  - Sara/Finlytics: sign-off on prompt pack + procurement OK for pilot nodes
  - Marissa: set up pilot and coordinate benchmarks
  - Ben & Karthik: finalize canary config and fallback routing rules

Attachments: finlytics_benchmarks_20270718.csv (bench marks), finlytics_prompt_pack_v1.txt (prompt/test cases), canary_playbook_mup.md (deployment steps)

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync tomorrow to walk through the benchmarks.

Best,
Marissa

Sara / Alex —

Thanks for the quick review. Short answers below and next steps attached: 

1) Latency (RW-13B-q4): p50 ~85ms, p95 ~360ms at sustained 5 QPS with batching + KV cache warm. Cold-starts (scale-up) can add ~80–120ms; we'll include a warm pool for user-facing routes to avoid that. See finlytics_benchmarks_20270718.csv for distribution.

2) Hallucination precision: we define as percent of claims anchored to a verified retrieval token span. Primary automation is our evaluators (unit tests in attached prompt pack) + a factuality classifier. We attach the 20-case prioritized set (finlytics_prompt_pack_v1.txt) — marked top-5 failure modes. We'll run the eval harness nightly during the pilot and surface any drop >3% vs baseline as automatic stop-and-roll-back.

3) Licensing/marketplace: OpenLlama-30B-int8 weights are community-redistributable; procurement should note runtime third-party libs (we list them in the playbook). No additional DocuSign for the model itself. If you want a hosted Dedicated commit, we can include a marketplace addendum for managed nodes.

Proposed pilot cadence:
- Week 0: sign-off & procurement OK
- Week 1: deploy RW-13B-q4 primary, OpenLlama-30B-int8 canary (5% traffic)
- Week 2: expand canary to 20% if quality metrics show improvement, finalize rollback thresholds
